Goldfish Lab — Styleguide

The binding visual reference. Normative rules live in DESIGN.md; this document renders them.

Generated from assets/css/input.css by scripts/build_styleguide.py — do not edit by hand. 43 colour tokens, 19 enforced role pairings, worst measured contrast 5.11:1 (AA needs 4.5:1).

Grounding

A measurement instrument dressed as an old grimoire. It must feel like the Magic cards it simulates — pre-2003 dark fantasy, a tan scroll textbox on near-black leather — and read like a tool whose numbers you would trust.

The atmosphere carries the chrome: header, panels, buttons, empty states. Data itself is set plainly.

Wordmark & header

Goldfish Lab it actually plays your deck

Wordmark in the display serif, no logotype image. The tagline is the product claim and is never changed for decoration.

Typography

Display — EB Garamond
Subheading

Body text. EB Garamond, self-hosted, SIL Open Font License. Old-style proportions match the type on a pre-2003 card. Italic for emphasis. Semibold for labels.

Accented glyphs load from the latin-ext subset only when needed: Lim-Dûl, Æther.

Numbers use tabular figures. A report is a wall of percentages; proportional digits make columns ragged.

MilestoneR3R5 R6
Commander in play5.9 % 67.9 %84.4 %
Sacrifice engine4.1 % 11.9 %18.0 %
Coffers + Urborg1.0 % 1.7 %2.1 %

Percentages right-aligned, labels left-aligned, no zebra striping.

Buttons — all states

One primary action per view. Focus ring is 2px blood-700 with offset, on every focusable element.

Form fields

Your plan allows up to 10,000 games per run.
This field is required.

Panels & badges

Parchment surface

Cards, report panels, the playtest table. The default surface for anything the user reads closely.

Raised dark panel

Secondary information on the page ground. Used sparingly.

Modelled Treated as vanilla Needs review

Each badge carries a word. Colour is never the only carrier of meaning — the honesty layer has to reach a colour-blind reader too.

The honesty callout

What this simulation did not model

17 of your 99 cards have effects the engine cannot represent. They are treated as vanilla permanents: they cost mana and do nothing else.

Opponent-dependent cards such as Rhystic Study are worth exactly zero in a goldfish, and will simulate far worse than they play.

This pattern appears beside every result. It is the product's core differentiator, not a disclaimer to be tucked away.

Markers, bars and “More” (Phase 9, Paket 3)

! 3 cards need you ✓ Ready

3 of 5 decks More

The deck marker, a usage bar and the small “More” link, after a sentence that says why the section matters (never a “Why?” to answer). Each says it in words as well: the marker is a sentence, the bar has its count beside it, and blood-700 fills a bar only when the limit is reached. The card grid, the line charts and the playtest hand are described in DESIGN.md (“Pictures, markers and charts”) and live at their templates; this file shows the tokens they are built from.

“In short”: next to the precons (Paket 3)

4 lands by turn 4 81% Ahead of 3 of 5 precons. The precons’ middle: 76%.

Each number of “In short” beside the precons’: a faint tick per precon, one tall verdigris mark for the deck, and the same in words under it. Under five precons the block is left out.

Motion (Phase 10)

Keeping a two-lander. Living dangerously.

While a run plays, and only then: the fish swims a circle in the flask, bubbles rise, and one loading line beside it changes every three to five seconds with a 600 ms fade. The progress bar glides to each new value in 900 ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion all of it stands still: a still logo, one line, a bar that steps. The shapes are the favicon's; only the colours moved into tokens.

On the home page the header's fish is alive (static/js/fish.js): one short move now and then while nobody touches the page - a glance, a turn, rarely a jump out of the flask - and a click tilts the flask. Every move ends inside 2 s; under reduced motion only the eye widens, on a click.

Info symbols: the line in the text’s colour, one fill from gold, water, blood or verdigris, darker on parchment. Always beside their word, never a target of their own. Point at one (or tab to it): it moves once, under a second; never under reduced motion. Functional icons - the pencil, the bin, the padlock - stay one colour and sit in a button or link.

Tactics

Every title in the deck summary has its colour and its word, and every strength or weakness its + or −. A mechanism chip wears the swatch of its line in “What you drew”; the words say what it is.

Deck summary

Run a simulation to fill this. The summary is written with your first run.

The summary and “Your strategies” stand on the deck page under the tiles (Paket 2): they are the deck’s, not one run’s. Without a run the block is there with one line that links to Simulate. The report keeps “Combos & engines” and links back to the summary.

Deck list values (Paket 2)

UB Bracket 3+ simulated 03.11.26

Each deck in “Your decks” says three things under its name: its colour identity as pips in WUBRG order (named for a screen reader), the bracket exactly as the deck page’s tile says it (one shared include), and when it was last simulated, linking to that run, or “not simulated yet”. One quiet row; more decks never mean more queries.

On Off

“Your decks”: the commander small, the deck’s three most expensive spells fanned out to the right behind it, turned about their bottom edge (.deck-fan). Pictures only: hidden from screen readers, the name beside it says the same. A setting is a .switch: a real button with role="switch", a dark track when on, and always the word On or Off beside it.

Theme chips: “Built around” (Themen-Doc, Paket 1)

Aristocrats · strong Typal Zombie · medium Graveyard · hinted

A theme is a chip that opens (.deck-theme, a <details>, no script). The level is always the word on the chip; the border only repeats it: thick and filled for strong, solid for medium, dashed for hinted. An open theme takes the whole row and lists each piece as “8, wants 6” with its cards; the number sits folded under “Advanced”. No theme is said in a sentence, never guessed.

Engines and synergies: “Combos & engines” (Themen-Doc, Paket 1)

Viscera Seer + Blood Artist + Bitterblossom

Aristocrats · strong

Viscera Seer sacrifices, Blood Artist pays off each death, Bitterblossom brings more bodies.

Get Bitterblossom out first, then the Seer; keep Blood Artist back until a board wipe is unlikely. Written by Mistral AI. It can be wrong.

Running by turn 6 in 41% of games, in your last run.

Zealous Conscripts

Theft · hinted

1 of 2 pieces. Still missing: Sacrifices what it took

An engine is a row with a rule at its left, as a combo is: its cards, its theme and level as words, one sentence of what each card does. A piece short, the rule is dashed and the row names what is missing; the dash only repeats the words. Pairs show the five strongest open and the rest in one fold, each with its numbers under “Advanced”. Under a complete engine, by which turn it runs in the last run (PR 5), the share in bold; not measured yet, the line says the next run will. How an engine plays (PR 6) comes from the deck summary: Mistral's sentence under the rules' one, followed by “Written by Mistral AI. It can be wrong.” in ink-700, only while the engine still has the cards it was written about.

Lock-in: locked, dismissed, resting (Themen-Doc, Paket 1, PR 4)

Viscera Seer + Blood Artist

🔒 Locked Unlock

Aristocrats · strong

Ashnod's Altar + Grave Pact

🔒 Locked

Resting, a card is missing: Grave Pact. It is back when the card is.

Chainer + Entomb

🔒 ×

▸ 1 dismissed

Only what the owner says is stored. A suggestion has two small square buttons, a padlock and a cross, each named in full for a screen reader. A locked entry says “Locked” with the padlock and comes first, and it stays even when the rules no longer find it. A dismissed one leaves the list for a fold at the end, “1 dismissed”, where it can be brought back. An entry whose card left the deck turns ink-700 and says which card. The dashed rule keeps its one meaning, a piece short; locking never changes the rule.

Do & Don't

Do

  • Set data plainly. Atmosphere belongs in the chrome, not behind a table of percentages.
  • Right-align percentages, left-align labels, and use tabular figures so columns line up.
  • Pair every state colour with a word. A hue alone is not a message.
  • Keep blood as an accent - a button, a rule, a badge.
  • Cap prose at about 70 characters. Tables may run full width.
  • Say what the simulation could not model, in the same panel as the result.

Don't

  • Six accent colours and a donut chart per metric. That is what every competitor looks like.
  • A full-width blood banner - it reads as an error page.
  • Parchment texture behind dense numeric data.
  • Pure black (#000) or pure white. The ground is warm near-black.
  • An inline hex value. A new meaning gets a step in an existing family, documented first.
  • Zebra striping on report tables - it fights the parchment texture.

Sync rule

DESIGN.md → STYLEGUIDE.html → assets/css/input.css → tests/test_design_tokens.py

Change the rule first, regenerate this file, then move the tokens, then extend the contrast test. Never edit a token first and document it afterwards.
